diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that the hyperbolic update is at least first-order accurate in time and space and subject to a hyperbolic CFL condition $\tau_n = \mathcal O(h)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The per-step residual bound is derived entirely from the assertion that the formal $\theta$-scheme density update $\tilde\rho_h^{n+\theta}$ and the actual computed state $\rho_h^{n+\theta}$ agree to $O(\tau_n^2)$; the paper itself states this would need to be verified in detail. No verification is given, and the estimate does not follow from the stated first-order-accuracy hypothesis alone, since it requires a consistency analysis comparing the $\theta$-scheme mass update (with the source-update velocity) against the concrete hyperbolic solver's mass update. The telescoped rates of Corollary \ref{cor:added-3} inherit the same unverified step.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Carry out the contained truncation-error verification for the concrete hyperbolic solver (the implementation uses a third-order Runge--Kutta scheme, for which the $O(\tau_n^2)$ closeness is plausible), or relabel the proposition as a heuristic estimate.

issues.failure_explanation: The reduction factor $\{1-\max(0,\delta\mathcal E^{n+1}/\mathcal E_{\text{kin}}^{n+1})\}^{1/2}$ takes the square root of a negative number whenever the restart raises the potential energy by more than the available kinetic energy ($\delta\mathcal E^{n+1}>\mathcal E_{\text{kin}}^{n+1}>0$), and divides by $\mathcal E_{\text{kin}}^{n+1}$; the update is therefore not well-defined on this part of its input domain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Cap the factor, e.g. $\max\big(0,1-\delta\mathcal E^{n+1}/\mathcal E_{\text{kin}}^{n+1}\big)^{1/2}$ (and define the update as $\vec m^{n+1}=0$ when $\mathcal E_{\text{kin}}^{n+1}=0$ with $\delta\mathcal E^{n+1}>0$); a one-line fix.
issues.overall_effect: The relaxation post-processing step can be ill-defined in corner cases; the full-restart definition and the energy-balance restoration intent are unaffected.
issues.title: Gauß-law restart with relaxation is ill-defined when the potential-energy increase exceeds the kinetic energy
issues.why_classification: A degenerate corner case with a local guard; the procedure's guarantees are unchanged.
